gnosh attach

  Open the agent view on a session that runs in the background. As Claude
  Code's claude attach: the session is a run that gnosh --bg, /background or
  /fork started, named by its ID, the start of one, or its name (gnosh agents
  lists them). A working run is watched as it goes, one that waits on a
  question shows the question, and one that is over opens as gnosh -r opens
  it. It needs a terminal; elsewhere gnosh logs -f follows a run.

  Not built yet in this build of gnosh: typing it stops with a message that
  says so.

Usage
  gnosh attach [flags] <session>

Flags
  --cwd <dir>
      Work in this folder instead of the current one.
  -h, --help
      Show help: gnosh's, or after a command's name that command's.
